page: Google Cloud Platform x4-480-6t-metal is a bare-metal, memory-optimized compute instance designed for heavy enterprise computing tasks. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and provides 480 dedicated vCPUs. The hardware configuration couples these cores with 6,144 GB of total system RAM, establishing a high memory density of 12.8 GB per core. The server contains no integrated GPUs.

Storage and network characteristics reflect a specialized bare-metal implementation. The x4-480-6t-metal has no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached storage or persistent disks for all filesystem requirements. Furthermore, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned directly to the machine. By providing bare-metal dedicated CPU allocation without hypervisor layers, the server eliminates virtualization contention across its 480 execution cores.

The hardware configuration is engineered for enterprise-scale in-memory computing requirements. Workload fit includes ultra-large relational and non-relational database systems, large SAP HANA deployments, high-throughput in-memory data caches, and massive enterprise transactional analytics where dataset sizes reach multiple terabytes and require persistent retention in RAM.
description: Google Cloud Platform x4-480-6t-metal is a bare-metal memory-optimized server configuration designed for extremely large memory footprints and compute-intensive enterprise workloads. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it delivers 480 dedicated vCPUs and 6,144 GB of physical system memory, establishing a high density of 12.8 GB of RAM per processing core. The system does not include onboard GPUs and features no local drive storage, requiring external or network-attached persistent storage for filesystem operations. Additionally, zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses are provisioned by default. By offering bare-metal access without hypervisor contention, the instance provides uninhibited execution of high-capacity processing threads. The x4-480-6t-metal is primarily suited for mission-critical enterprise platforms, massive in-memory databases like SAP HANA, large-scale distributed analytics, and complex datasets that require multi-terabyte system memory arrays to operate efficiently.
